summary.text: David Cook is a Republican former state representative running for the Arizona House of Representatives, District 7, in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A co-founder of the DC Cattle Company, he previously served in the House and chaired its Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.

paragraphs.text: Cook was born in Ponca City, Oklahoma, and graduated from Miami High School.
His career includes co-founding the DC Cattle Company and working as a sergeant with the Arizona Department of Corrections.
He has held leadership roles in the Arizona Cattle Growers' Association and the National Cattlemen's Beef Association, including as federal lands chairman of each.
Cook served in the Arizona House of Representatives from 2017 to 2025 and did not seek re-election in 2024.
In the 2023-2024 session he served on the Education, Land, Agriculture, and Rural Affairs, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees, chairing the last.
He advanced from the Republican primary on July 21, 2026.
In December 2018, KTAR reported, the Arizona Department of Public Safety stopped Cook in Mesa and he was arrested and charged with DUI; a breath test showed a blood alcohol content of .158.
Cook said in a Facebook post that he "learned a valuable lesson the hard way."

Fronteras Desk later reported that he pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor DUI charge and was sentenced to 24 hours in jail and a five-year probation period, with alcohol treatment, a victim-impact panel and a requirement to avoid drinking to excess.
